# Shanios Blog

> The official blog for Shanios — the immutable Linux OS with atomic blue-green updates, instant rollback, and zero telemetry. Engineering breakdowns, release notes, guides, and stories from the team building India's immutable Linux OS.

Primary image: https://shani.dev/assets/images/gnome-screenshot.jpg
All posts are also available as full-content HTML at https://blog.shani.dev/post/<slug>/ and in the complete corpus at https://blog.shani.dev/llms-full.txt

## Deep Dive

- [Inside the Shanios Build Pipeline: From Package List to Bootable Image](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-build-pipeline/): Every Shanios release starts as a list of package names and ends as a GPG-signed, Secure Boot-ready ISO. The build pipeline that bridges tho…
- [NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPUs on Shanios: How Drivers Work on an Immutable OS](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-gpu-drivers/): Ask any long-time Linux desktop user about graphics drivers and you will hear war stories: the kernel update that landed before the NVIDIA m…
- [Shani OS vs Fedora Silverblue, Bazzite, SteamOS, and NixOS — An Honest Comparison](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-vs-alternatives/): An honest technical comparison of immutable Linux distributions. Where Shani OS wins, where others genuinely win, and how to pick the right one for your situation. Btrfs send/receive vs OSTree vs OCI images, gaming focus, enterprise needs, and declarative vs imperative philosophy.
- [Apptainer (Singularity) on Shani OS — HPC Containers for Workstation and Cluster](https://blog.shani.dev/post/apptainer-on-shani-os/): Apptainer is the HPC standard for portable, reproducible containers — pre-installed on Shani OS, no root required, runs the same SIF image on your workstation and on any SLURM/PBS cluster. Build once, run anywhere, with full NVIDIA and AMD ROCm GPU support.
- [gen-efi and Secure Boot on Shani OS — UKI Generation, MOK Enrollment, and TPM2](https://blog.shani.dev/post/gen-efi-and-secure-boot/): gen-efi is the tool that builds and signs Unified Kernel Images, manages MOK keys for Secure Boot, and enrolls LUKS keys into TPM2. This is the complete reference for every gen-efi operation and the Secure Boot chain on Shani OS.
- [Security Without Configuration — How Shani OS Protects You by Default](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-security-deep-dive/): Six Linux Security Modules running simultaneously, an immutable root that survives root access, TPM2-sealed encryption, and zero telemetry. Here is exactly how each layer works and why it is on by default.
- [The Architecture Behind Shani OS — Subvolumes, Slots, and the Update Pipeline](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-architecture-deep-dive/): A detailed walkthrough of how Shani OS is structured on disk — every Btrfs subvolume, every mount, every step from image signing to your running desktop.
- [Why Your OS Update Should Never Break Your Computer — And How Shani OS Fixes This](https://blog.shani.dev/post/why-os-updates-should-never-break/): Every server admin knows: you never update the live system. You update the standby, verify it, then switch. Desktops never got this lesson — until now.

## Ecosystem

- [LXC and LXD on Shani OS — Full System Containers](https://blog.shani.dev/post/lxc-lxd-on-shani-os/): LXC and LXD run full Linux system containers on Shani OS — complete OS environments sharing the host kernel, stored in dedicated @lxc and @lxd Btrfs subvolumes that survive every OS update. Lighter than VMs, more complete than Distrobox.
- [systemd-nspawn and machinectl on Shani OS — Lightweight System Containers](https://blog.shani.dev/post/systemd-nspawn-on-shani-os/): systemd-nspawn is the lightest way to run a full Linux system environment on Shani OS — no image management, no daemon, no setup. Containers boot in under a second, live in the @machines Btrfs subvolume, and survive every OS update untouched.
- [Kubernetes on Shani OS — From a Single Node to a Production-Grade Cluster](https://blog.shani.dev/post/kubernetes-on-shani-os/): Shani OS and Kubernetes are built for each other. Immutable OS root, Btrfs subvolumes, and fully decoupled lifecycles make it the ideal base for running k3s, RKE2, and the full modern stack — Cilium, ArgoCD, Longhorn, cert-manager, and beyond.
- [Snap on Shani OS — The Optional App Ecosystem](https://blog.shani.dev/post/snap-on-shani-os/): Snap is pre-configured on Shani OS with its own @snapd Btrfs subvolume. When to use Snap versus Flatpak, how to install from the Snap Store, and how the two ecosystems coexist.
- [Homebrew on Shani OS — For macOS Switchers and Those Who Prefer It](https://blog.shani.dev/post/homebrew-on-shani-os/): Homebrew works on Shani OS exactly as it does on macOS — install it once, use brew install for any of the thousands of formulae. A comparison with Nix to help you choose, and how both coexist.
- [Podman and Containers on Shani OS — Rootless, Docker-Compatible, Ready at Boot](https://blog.shani.dev/post/podman-containers-on-shani-os/): How to use Podman on Shani OS for rootless containers, Docker Compose workflows, and containerised services — with the Pods GUI, persistent storage in @containers, and full compatibility with the Docker ecosystem.
- [Distrobox on Shani OS — A Full Mutable Linux Inside an Immutable One](https://blog.shani.dev/post/distrobox-on-shani-os/): How to use Distrobox to run any Linux distribution inside Shani OS — full pacman, apt, dnf, AUR helpers, and GUI apps — without touching the immutable host OS. With BoxBuddy for graphical management.
- [Flatpak on Shani OS — Your Complete App Management Guide](https://blog.shani.dev/post/flatpak-on-shani-os/): How Flatpak works on Shani OS, what apps are pre-installed, how to install more from Flathub, manage permissions with Flatseal, and why sandboxing is the right model for an immutable system.
- [Nix on Shani OS — The Best Package Manager for an Immutable System](https://blog.shani.dev/post/nix-on-shani-os/): Why Nix and immutable Linux are a natural match, how to set it up on Shani OS in five minutes, and practical workflows for developers, researchers, and power users.

## Enterprise

- [Shani OS for OEMs and IT Fleets — Deploy Once, Maintain Never](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-oem-and-fleet-deployment/): How Shani OS eliminates per-device drift, enables one-command remote rollback, automates firmware updates, and makes fleet management genuinely simple — whether you are an OEM shipping hardware or an IT team managing hundreds of machines.

- [Use Shanios Tools on Any Arch-Based Distro](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-repo-on-other-distros/): Shanios builds tools that are useful beyond its own filesystem layout. gen-efi generates Secure Boot UKIs for any Arch system. shani-health …
- [Leaving Windows or macOS for Shanios: The Complete Switcher's Guide](https://blog.shani.dev/post/switching-from-windows-and-macos/): Every week I hear the same two sentences. From Windows users: "I'm done with updates breaking my machine." From Mac users: "The hardware is …
- [Android App Compatibility on Shani OS — What Works, What Doesn't, and Workarounds](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-android-app-compatibility/): Which Android apps work in Waydroid on Shani OS — Indian banking and government apps, streaming services, DRM status, and practical workarounds for apps that are blocked. Includes a tested compatibility list for common Indian apps.
- [Your First Week with Shani OS — From Install to Fully Set Up](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-first-week/): A day-by-day walkthrough for new Shani OS users: getting encryption and updates sorted on day one, then systematically setting up email, cloud sync, printing, dev tools, backups, and daily habits through the first week.
- [Shani OS for Designers and Visual Creators — Photo Editing, Vector, UI Design, and 3D](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-for-designers-and-visual-creators/): A complete guide for photographers, illustrators, UI/UX designers, 3D artists, and visual creators on Shani OS — GIMP, Inkscape, Krita, Blender, Darktable, RawTherapee, Figma via browser, colour management, display calibration, and tablet support. Everything works at first boot.
- [Shani OS for General Desktop Users — Productivity, Office, Web, and Everyday Use](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-for-general-desktop-users/): Shani OS for everyday desktop use — office suite and document compatibility, web browsing, email, video calls, cloud storage, calendar, notes, PDF tools, and everything a student, office worker, or home user needs. Most of it works from first boot.
- [Shani OS for Video Creators and Content Creators — Editing, Colour, Streaming, and Podcasting](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-for-video-creators/): The complete video production stack on Shani OS — DaVinci Resolve, Kdenlive, OpenShot, OBS Studio for streaming and recording, Audacity and Ardour for audio, GPU-accelerated encoding, and everything a YouTuber, podcaster, or video editor needs from first boot.
- [Multimedia on Shani OS — Codecs, Media Players, Streaming, and Hardware Decoding](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-multimedia/): Everything multimedia on Shani OS — hardware-accelerated video decode for Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA, codec support, streaming services with Widevine DRM, MPV and VLC, media servers, DLNA/Chromecast, and managing a media library with Jellyfin or Plex.
- [Running Windows Apps on Shani OS — Wine, Bottles, and When to Use a VM](https://blog.shani.dev/post/windows-apps-on-shani-os/): You do not need Windows to run Windows software on Shani OS. Bottles (pre-installed on the KDE Plasma edition) manages Wine environments for productivity tools, creative software, and legacy apps. Here is how to get any Windows app running, and when a VM is the better answer.
- [GPU Compute on Shani OS — NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, and Intel oneAPI](https://blog.shani.dev/post/gpu-compute-on-shani-os/): How to run GPU compute workloads on Shani OS — setting up AMD ROCm with PyTorch and TensorFlow via Distrobox, NVIDIA CUDA via Distrobox, Intel oneAPI, HIP for cross-vendor portability, and Nix for pure ML environments. Works for ML, simulation, data science, and scientific computing.
- [System Configuration on Shani OS — /etc, Services, and What Persists](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-system-configuration/): The /etc OverlayFS on Shani OS means all your configuration changes persist normally across every OS update and rollback. This guide covers editing config files, managing systemd services, enabling services, kernel parameters, and inspecting what you have customised.
- [Audio on Shani OS — PipeWire, WirePlumber, JACK, and Professional Audio](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-audio-pipewire/): Shani OS uses PipeWire 1.4.x as its audio stack — simultaneously compatible with ALSA, PulseAudio, and JACK. This guide covers everyday audio management, Bluetooth codec selection, fixing common issues, and setting up low-latency professional audio workflows.
- [KDE Connect and GSConnect on Shani OS — Your Phone and Desktop, Together](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-kde-connect/): KDE Connect (KDE edition) and GSConnect (GNOME edition) link your Android phone to your Shani OS desktop — notifications mirrored, files shared, clipboard synced, remote input, SMS from desktop, and media control. Firewall rules are pre-configured.
- [Indian Language Support on Shani OS — Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, and More](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-indian-language-support/): Indian language support on Shani OS is designed in from the start — not bolted on. Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi, Bengali, and more: correct font rendering, IBus multilingual input, and Indian-English locale all configured at first boot.
- [AppImage on Shani OS — Portable Apps with Gear Lever](https://blog.shani.dev/post/appimage-on-shani-os/): AppImages are self-contained portable executables that need no installation and work on any Linux system. Gear Lever (pre-installed) integrates them into your desktop launcher, manages updates, and keeps them in persistent storage that survives OS updates.
- [Accessibility on Shani OS — Screen Reader, Braille, Magnification, and More](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-accessibility/): Shani OS ships a complete accessibility stack at first boot — Orca screen reader with espeak-ng TTS, braille display support via brltty, display magnification, high-contrast themes, keyboard navigation, and assistive technology infrastructure. Nothing to install.
- [Btrfs Snapshots and Backup on Shani OS — Protecting Your Data the Right Way](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-btrfs-snapshots-and-backup/): How to use Btrfs snapshots for instant point-in-time copies of your home directory, and how to set up real off-device backups with restic and rclone — both pre-installed on Shani OS. Snapshots are not backups. Here is the difference and how to do both.
- [Bluetooth on Shani OS — Headphones, Controllers, File Transfer, and Pairing](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-bluetooth/): Bluetooth on Shani OS works at first boot for audio, gaming controllers, keyboards, mice, file transfer, and tethering. Paired devices persist across every OS update and rollback. Here is everything you need to know.
- [Printing and Scanning on Shani OS — CUPS, Driverless Printing, and SANE](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-printing-and-scanning/): How printing and scanning work on Shani OS — driverless IPP-over-USB and network discovery, CUPS configuration, manufacturer-specific drivers for HP, Brother, Canon, and scanner setup via SANE and sane-airscan.
- [Power Management on Shani OS — Hibernation, Suspend, Battery Life, and Profiles](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-power-management/): Shani OS configures hibernation automatically at install, manages power profiles out of the box, and handles TPM2-sealed LUKS so the disk unlocks silently on your own hardware. Everything a laptop user needs — with nothing to configure.
- [Shani OS as a Home Server — Self-Host Everything, No Public IP Required](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-home-server/): Turn any PC, mini PC, or old laptop into a home server that replaces your cloud subscriptions. Media streaming, AI models, file sync, home automation, password management, and a full education platform — all accessible from anywhere, with no public IP and no port forwarding.
- [Networking on Shani OS — VPNs, Tailscale, SSH, Caddy, and More](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-networking-guide/): A practical guide to every network capability built into Shani OS — from WireGuard and Tailscale mesh VPNs to Caddy reverse proxy, SSH hardening, Cloudflare tunnels, LAN file sharing, brute-force protection, and enterprise services.
- [The Shell Experience on Shani OS — Zsh, Starship, McFly, FZF, and More](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-shell-and-terminal/): Shani OS ships a fully configured, modern shell environment — Zsh with syntax highlighting and autosuggestions, Starship prompt, McFly neural-network history, FZF fuzzy search, and a complete toolkit of CLI tools. Here is how it all fits together.
- [Running Android Apps on Shani OS with Waydroid](https://blog.shani.dev/post/waydroid-android-on-shani-os/): Waydroid runs a full hardware-accelerated Android stack inside a lightweight container on Shani OS — full Play Store access, ARM app compatibility, and native GPU performance. Here is how to set it up and get the most out of it.
- [Shani OS for Researchers and HPC — Reproducible Environments from Desktop to Cluster](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-for-researchers-and-hpc/): How Shani OS makes scientific computing reproducible from the ground up — Apptainer for cluster workloads, Nix for pinned environments, AMD ROCm and NVIDIA CUDA via Distrobox containers, DVC for data versioning, and a GPG-signed host OS that is itself a verifiable artefact.
- [Gaming on Shani OS — The Full Stack, Explained](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-gaming-deep-dive/): Everything pre-installed on the KDE Plasma edition and why it matters: Steam + Proton, MangoHud, GameScope, Ananicy, kernel tuning, NVIDIA setup, peripheral support, and why immutability makes Shani OS the most reliable gaming OS on Linux.
- [Virtual Machines on Shani OS — QEMU/KVM, virt-manager, GPU Passthrough, and Windows VMs](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-virtual-machines/): How to run fast, hardware-accelerated VMs on Shani OS — setting up KVM with virt-manager, running Windows with VirtIO drivers, GPU passthrough for gaming or ML, and why the @libvirt subvolume keeps your VMs safe across every OS update.
- [Shani OS for Everyone — Find Your Guide](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-for-everyone/): Shani OS works for Windows and macOS switchers, developers, gamers, and IT administrators. This page points you to the right guide for your situation.
- [Getting Started with Shani OS — From Download to Daily Use](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-getting-started/): A complete walkthrough: download, verify, install, and configure Shani OS from scratch — including Flatpak apps, Nix packages, Distrobox containers, and TPM2 encryption setup.

## Migration

- [Migrating to Shani OS from Ubuntu, Fedora, or Arch — A Practical Guide](https://blog.shani.dev/post/migrating-to-shani-os/): A workflow-by-workflow migration guide for users coming from traditional mutable Linux distributions. Every pacman, apt, and dnf habit has a clean equivalent on Shani OS — here is the full map.

## Reference

- [shani-health — System Health Monitoring for Shani OS](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-health-reference/): shani-health is the CLI tool for checking the health of a running Shani OS system — boot state, security posture, storage, network, hardware, and a deep integrity check with machine-readable output. Introduced in the 2026.04.15 release.
- [Shani OS FAQ — Frequently Asked Questions](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-faq/): Answers to the most common questions about Shani OS: software installation, what happens to your files after rollback, hardware compatibility, dual boot, gaming, security, and the immutable model in plain terms.
- [The Shani OS Software Ecosystem — What to Use, When, and Why](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-software-ecosystem/): One canonical reference for every software installation option on Shani OS: Flatpak, Snap, AppImage, Nix, Distrobox, Podman, LXC/LXD, systemd-nspawn, Apptainer, Homebrew, and VMs. Includes a decision flowchart, full comparison table, and the subvolume each ecosystem lives in.
- [Shani OS Troubleshooting Guide — Boot, Updates, Audio, GPU, and More](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-troubleshooting-guide/): The consolidated troubleshooting reference for Shani OS — boot failures and slot recovery, update issues, audio problems, Bluetooth, Flatpak sandbox, NVIDIA detection, TPM2 unlock, Waydroid, and common journalctl commands for diagnosing anything else.
- [Updates on Shani OS — shani-update, shani-deploy, and the Full Reference](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-updates/): The complete guide to Shani OS updates: how shani-update detects and surfaces updates automatically, and the full shani-deploy flag reference for every scenario — update, rollback, dry-run, cleanup, channel management, and automated fleet deployments.
- [shani-update — The Shani OS Update Manager](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-update-notifications/): shani-update is the user-facing update manager for Shani OS. It runs automatically via a systemd user timer and at login, detects boot failures, checks for...
- [LUKS2 Encryption on Shani OS — Setup, Management, and Recovery](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-os-luks-after-installation/): Full-disk encryption must be enabled at install time on Shani OS. This guide covers what to do if you missed it, and the complete reference for managing LUKS2 on an already-encrypted system: keyslots, passphrases, keyfiles, header backup, TPM2, and emergency recovery.
- [shani-deploy Reference — Every Flag, Every Workflow](https://blog.shani.dev/post/shani-deploy-reference/): The complete reference for shani-deploy — the atomic update and rollback tool at the heart of Shani OS. Every flag, every use case, every edge case covered: update, rollback, dry-run, cleanup, optimize, channel management, and more.
